items.description: 2027 skills.

skills.name: agent-hiring-panel
skills.description: Hire an AI agent the way you'd hire an employee — a role spec with success criteria, a structured work-sample interview run on your real tasks, reference checks (what do actual users report), probation KPIs, and termination criteria written before day one.

skills.name: agent-severance
skills.description: Offboard an AI agent the way you'd offboard an employee — inventory what it knew and touched, export then purge its memory, revoke every credential and access grant, and write the handover for its successor (human or agent).

skills.name: ai-disclosure-policy
skills.description: Decide when and how your product and communications must (or should) label AI-generated content, and write the disclosure policy — surface-by-surface rules, exact label wording, and the review trigger for regulations like the EU AI Act's transparency obligations.

skills.name: api-for-yourself
skills.description: Publish 'how to work with me' as a literal API spec — endpoints (what to ask me for and what you'll get back), rate limits (meeting and interrupt tolerance), error codes (what happens when you surprise me Friday 5pm), auth (how to earn trust), and a changelog.

skills.name: clone-brief
skills.description: Send your position to a meeting instead of your body — a one-page brief carrying your stances, fallbacks, red lines, tradables, and delegation limits, readable by the colleague (or agent) representing you.

skills.name: context-bankruptcy
skills.description: Declare bankruptcy on a long-lived AI agent's accumulated memory — audit what it currently believes, separate ground truth from stale and wrong, purge deliberately, restate the truths that survive, and log what was lost.

skills.name: deepfake-drill
skills.description: Run a tabletop drill of a voice-clone or deepfake fraud attempt — the 'CEO needs this wire today' call — against your actual approval process, before a real attacker does, then debrief the tells and fix the process gap.

skills.name: the-org-simulator
skills.description: Stress-test a proposed org change before announcing it — simulate who gains, who loses, who blocks, where friction erupts in the first 90 days, and run the memo leak test: how does this land when it leaks before you announce it? Use when planning a reorg, changing reporting lines, merging or splitting teams, moving a function, or 'how will this org change land?'.

skills.name: the-time-capsule
skills.description: Write a sealed memo to your future self or successor — the honest state of things, falsifiable predictions with confidence levels, and the advice you suspect they'll need — with an open-on date and a scoring ritual for when it's opened.

skills.name: the-understudy
skills.description: Study 3-5 samples of the user's real writing and decisions, build an explicit 'how you think' profile, then draft new work as their understudy — always with a 'what I couldn't infer about you' list so the gaps are visible instead of guessed.

items.description: Topic in, interactive 3D explorer out: the interface brief and mock prompt, image-to-3D prompts with a sourced parts list, a single-file Three.js viewer with clickable labelled parts, exploded view and quiz mode, and a pipeline that runs them in order

skills.name: explorer-interface-brief
skills.description: Use when asked to design the interface for an interactive 3D explorer, plan a UI for exploring a 3D model of a topic, or write an image-model prompt for a 3D learning app mock-up.

skills.name: explorer-pipeline
skills.description: Use when asked to make an interactive 3D explorer of a topic from start to finish, go from a topic to a clickable 3D learning page, or run the whole 3D explorer process.

skills.name: explorer-viewer-builder
skills.description: Use when asked to build a 3D viewer for a GLB model, make an interactive explorer with clickable labelled parts, add an exploded view or quiz to a 3D model, or turn a parts list into a web page.

skills.name: model-prompt-pack
skills.description: Use when asked to write prompts for image-to-3D or text-to-3D tools, generate 3D models of a topic's parts, plan the assets for a 3D explorer, or build a labelled parts list with sources.

items.description: Accessibility skills.

skills.name: accessible-travel-planner
skills.description: Plan a trip that actually works with a disability or access need — confirm real accessibility (not just 'accessible' labels), book the assistance in advance, plan for equipment and medication, and build in the contingencies for when access breaks down.

skills.name: accommodation-request
skills.description: Request a reasonable accommodation at work or in education — frame it around the barrier and the adjustment (not your diagnosis), cite the right process, and navigate the back-and-forth constructively.

skills.name: disability-benefit-appeal
skills.description: Appeal a denied disability benefit (SSDI/SSI, PIP, DLA, ESA and similar) — decode the denial reason, build the evidence-backed case that answers it, hit the deadline, and prepare for the hearing.

skills.name: disability-disclosure-decision
skills.description: Decide whether, when, how, and to whom to disclose a disability or health condition at work — weighing the real benefits (accommodations, protection, honesty) against the real risks (bias, gossip), tuned to your specific situation.

skills.name: venue-access-check
skills.description: Check whether a specific venue — a restaurant, office, event space, Airbnb, clinic — will actually work for your access needs, before you commit, with the exact questions to ask and the red flags in the answers.

items.description: Accounting & bookkeeping skills for finance ops and small businesses: Invoice Generator, Expense Policy, Collections Email, Financial Statement Explainer, Bookkeeping Categorization, and Cash Flow Forecast. Practical money admin — drafting aids, not tax/accounting advice.

skills.name: bookkeeping-categorization
skills.description: Set up a chart of accounts and rules for categorizing transactions.

skills.name: cash-flow-forecast
skills.description: Build a short-term (13-week) cash flow forecast to see if you can cover what's due.

skills.name: collections-email
skills.description: Write a polite-but-firm payment-reminder / collections email sequence for overdue invoices.

skills.name: expense-policy
skills.description: Write a clear company expense & reimbursement policy.

skills.name: financial-statement-explainer
skills.description: Explain a financial statement (P&L, balance sheet, or cash flow) in plain English.

skills.name: invoice-generator
skills.description: Create a professional, complete invoice for a client or customer.

skills.name: voice-agent-design

skills.name: agent-observability-spec
skills.description: Specify the tracing, metrics, and alerting for an AI agent or LLM feature in production.

skills.name: ai-eval-plan

skills.name: context-engineering-review

skills.name: llm-cost-latency-budget

skills.name: model-migration-plan
skills.description: Plan the migration of an LLM feature from one model to another without breaking production.

skills.name: prompt-regression-suite
skills.description: Design a regression test suite that catches an LLM feature getting worse when the prompt, model, or context changes.

skills.description: Prepare the conversations with aging parents that everyone postpones — the driving talk, the money talk, the care-options talk, the moving talk — each with an opener that doesn't ambush, a dignity-first script, rehearsal against realistic resistance, and the fallback when it goes badly.

items.description: Skills for using AI itself well — picking the right tool, delegating to it, briefing it with context, designing AI workflows, verifying its output, and catching its mistakes.

skills.name: ai-agent-reliability
skills.description: Make an AI agent or automation reliable enough to trust — the tests, checks, and guardrails that catch its failures before they reach anything real.

skills.name: ai-context-primer
skills.description: Build the context an AI needs to do a task well — the background, constraints, examples, and format it can't guess — so you get a great result on the first try instead of a generic one you have to keep correcting.

skills.name: ai-output-verifier
skills.description: Check AI output before you trust or use it — where it's likely wrong, what to verify, and how to catch confident-sounding errors.

skills.name: ai-tool-picker
skills.description: Figure out which AI tool actually fits the task in front of you — chatbot, coding assistant, image model, agent, or none — instead of forcing one tool onto everything.

skills.name: ai-workflow-designer
skills.description: Design an AI-assisted workflow for a recurring task — which steps to hand to AI, which to keep human, and how they connect — so you get leverage without losing quality or control.

skills.name: claude-project-setup
skills.description: Set up a repo or project so an AI coding agent works well in it — the CLAUDE.md, the context, the guardrails, and the conventions the agent needs to be useful instead of lost.

skills.name: delegate-to-ai
skills.description: Decide what in your workload to hand to AI and what to keep yourself — like managing a fast, capable, but unreliable new hire — so you get leverage without offloading the things that need you.

skills.name: get-more-from-ai
skills.description: Level up how you actually use AI — from basic one-shot questions to the techniques that get dramatically better results — matched to what you already do.

skills.name: memory-file-maintenance
skills.description: Keep your AI memory/context file (MEMORY.md, CLAUDE.md, custom instructions) healthy over time — pruning the stale, adding the new, and keeping it sharp so your AI keeps getting you right.

skills.name: prompt-debugging
skills.description: Figure out why a prompt isn't working and fix it — diagnose the actual failure (ambiguity, missing context, wrong format, conflicting instructions) instead of randomly rewording.

skills.name: prompt-library-builder
skills.description: Build a personal library of reusable prompts for the things you ask AI again and again — so you stop rewriting the same request from scratch.

skills.name: run-an-agent-team
skills.description: Design a small team of AI agents to tackle a complex task in parallel — who does what, how they hand off, and how to keep them coordinated — instead of one overloaded agent doing everything serially.

skills.name: spot-ai-mistakes
skills.description: Learn to recognize where and how AI tends to go wrong — the specific failure patterns — so you catch its mistakes on sight instead of getting burned by confident errors.

skills.name: ai-assisted-performance-review
skills.description: Evaluate performance fairly when output is AI-assisted — what still measures the human, what now measures the tooling, and how to run the review conversation.

skills.name: ai-content-audit
skills.description: Audit a content library, docs site, or blog for AI-generated filler that's eroding trust and search performance — and triage what to fix, rewrite, or delete.

skills.name: ai-roi-audit
skills.description: Audit whether the organisation's AI spend actually paid — measured against baselines, not vendor math or vibes.

skills.name: ai-usage-policy
skills.description: Write an AI usage policy people can actually follow — approved tools, data rules, disclosure duties, and review obligations, in one page instead of legal fog.

skills.name: role-redesign-for-ai
skills.description: Redesign a job role that AI now does a large part of — deliberately, instead of quietly expecting the same headcount to absorb 140% output.

skills.name: architectural-programme-brief
skills.description: Turn a client's wishes into an architectural brief that can actually be designed against — the accommodation schedule, the adjacencies, the budget reality, and the constraints named before they become change orders.

skills.name: architectural-specification
skills.description: Write a specification section that a contractor can price accurately and a site can build from — performance stated, products defined, workmanship and tolerances given, and the coordination with the drawings made explicit.

skills.name: architecture-client-presentation

skills.name: construction-rfi-response

skills.name: planning-application-statement

skills.name: site-analysis-report
skills.description: Analyse a site before designing on it — what is physically there, what the law and the neighbours allow, and which constraints will actually shape the building.

skills.name: schedule-recipe
skills.description: Turn 'run this every Friday at 4pm' into a working, copy-paste schedule on the user's actual runner.

skills.name: credit-memo

skills.name: kyc-escalation

items.description: Executable business calculators & models — each ships a stdlib script: Unit Economics (LTV/CAC), SaaS Metrics (NRR/quick ratio), Runway (default alive/dead), Pricing, ROI/NPV — plus computed models that emit real .xlsx with live formulas: cohort curve fitting (LTV), Monte Carlo runway (P10/P50/P90), and Van Westendorp pricing. Verifiable math, not vibes.

skills.name: car-tco
skills.description: Compare the total cost of car ownership across buy-new, buy-used, lease, and keep-your-current-car — depreciation, insurance, maintenance ramp, and fuel over a real horizon, not just the monthly payment.

skills.name: cohort-curve-model
skills.description: Fit a retention curve to observed cohort data and project LTV — computed, not estimated.

skills.name: college-cost
skills.description: Compute what a degree will actually cost — sticker minus real aid, inflated per year, split into cash and loans, with the loan's decade-long monthly tail made visible before enrollment instead of after.

skills.name: daycare-vs-stay-home
skills.description: Run the real math on a parent leaving work versus paying for childcare — the second income net of daycare, marginal taxes, and work costs, AND the career-trajectory cost of years out, over horizons instead of one brutal year.

skills.name: debt-payoff
skills.description: Build a debt payoff plan — avalanche vs snowball simulated month by month on your actual debts, the real payoff dates, and the psychology-vs-arithmetic tradeoff priced in dollars.

skills.name: decision-tree-solver
skills.description: Turn a fork-in-the-road decision into a computed expected-value tree — settle or sue, launch or wait, fix or replace — rolled back by the bundled script, with the break-even probability where the answer flips.

skills.name: emergency-fund
skills.description: Size an emergency fund from essential spend and real risk factors — not a one-size 'six months' — with the funding timeline and where the money should sit.

skills.name: ev-vs-gas
skills.description: Compare an EV against a comparable gas car on total cost — upfront gap after incentives, energy vs fuel per year, maintenance delta, and the crossover year when the EV pulls ahead (or doesn't).

skills.name: exit-waterfall
skills.description: Compute who gets what at each exit price from a cap table — liquidation preferences, conversion points, and where the founders' share collapses.

skills.name: fair-split
skills.description: Divide things that cannot be divided — an inherited house, a dissolved partnership, the furniture after a breakup — using sealed-bid fair division (Knaster), computed by the bundled script so everyone ends provably above their own fair share.

skills.name: fire-number
skills.description: Compute a financial-independence (FIRE) target and years-to-reach with every assumption labeled as an assumption — plus a sensitivity table instead of a single false-precision answer.

skills.name: freelance-rate
skills.description: Derive a freelance day/hourly rate backwards from target income, honest billable utilization, overhead, and the self-employment tax premium — the arithmetic that proves a rate is not salary÷2000.

skills.name: offer-comparison
skills.description: Compare two or more job offers as total-comp curves over four years — vesting cliffs, bonuses, 401(k) match, and the crossover year computed, not vibed.

skills.name: pricing-calculator
skills.description: Model pricing scenarios — tiers, margins, break-even, and the revenue impact of a price change.

skills.name: pricing-sensitivity-model
skills.description: Van Westendorp price sensitivity, computed from real survey answers — crossings found by interpolation, not read off a chart by eye.

skills.name: raise-vs-jump
skills.description: Model staying for annual raises vs job-hopping for bigger bumps — cumulative earnings trajectories, the crossover year, and the costs the salary math hides (vesting resets, promotion paths, search risk).

skills.name: refinance-breakeven
skills.description: Compute the month a refinance actually starts saving money — payment delta, breakeven month, and total interest on both paths including the term-reset trap.

skills.name: rent-vs-buy
skills.description: Model rent-vs-buy honestly — year-by-year net position for both paths including the assumption everyone drops (the renter invests the difference), with a breakeven horizon instead of a verdict.

skills.name: roi-estimator
skills.description: Estimate the ROI, payback, and NPV of an investment, project, or purchase.

skills.name: runway-calculator
skills.description: Calculate cash runway, burn, and the zero-cash date — and whether you're default alive or dead.

skills.name: runway-monte-carlo
skills.description: Cash runway as a distribution, not a number — Monte Carlo simulated.

skills.name: saas-metrics
skills.description: Compute the core SaaS metrics — MRR/ARR, growth, NRR/GRR, churn, quick ratio, magic number — from your numbers.

skills.name: schedule-monte-carlo
skills.description: Project completion as a distribution, not a date — Monte Carlo over the task graph.

skills.name: solar-breakeven
skills.description: Model whether solar panels pay for themselves for your roof — net cost after incentives, bill offset with degradation, electricity inflation, the inverter replacement, and the breakeven year, plus the policy risk no calculator controls.

skills.name: student-loan-strategy
skills.description: Decide what the extra money does about student loans — attack them, invest alongside them, or ride a forgiveness track — with the three paths simulated on your actual loans and the guaranteed-vs-assumed framing kept honest.

skills.name: subscription-audit
skills.description: Find and rank the recurring-payment leak — every subscription annualized, sorted by real yearly cost, with the keep/cancel/downgrade pass and the where-they-hide checklist.

skills.name: support-staffing-model
skills.description: How many support agents does the queue actually need — Erlang C, computed, not 'tickets per agent' folklore.

skills.name: tornado-sensitivity
skills.description: Which assumption actually moves the answer — one-at-a-time sensitivity, ranked into a tornado.

skills.name: unit-economics
skills.description: Model the unit economics of a business — CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin — from real inputs.

skills.name: wedding-budget
skills.description: Build a wedding budget that survives to the wedding — allocation by real shares, the per-guest lever made explicit, the routinely-forgotten line items priced in from day one, and a contingency that isn't decorative.

skills.name: layoff-first-72-hours
